title: Viet Nam government implications of the ENSO revenue event assessment

claims.text: This assessment does not estimate infrastructure repair costs for Viet Nam. Its model scope is agriculture, forestry and fishing value added and the conditional transmission to government revenue; it measures the event-versus-neutral difference in government revenue, not spending on infrastructure repair or damage. No infrastructure repair cost quantity is present in the evidence packet, so none can be reported.

The tail shortfall figures are positive-part expected-shortfall measures applied to the revenue-loss distribution, and thus describe a conditional loss scenario for government revenue, not an infrastructure repair budget.

limitations: The assessment contains no infrastructure repair cost estimates for Viet Nam or any other country; the question cannot be answered with an infrastructure-specific number from this evidence.
The model scope is agriculture, forestry and fishing value added and conditional government revenue transmission; it explicitly does not measure total-economy loss, damage, or repair expenditure.
Mean revenue loss figures are signed (event minus neutral can be a gain in some draws); only the positive-part shortfall enters the tail measure.
The evidence is a fixed bounded packet; historical input provenance is incomplete and the assessment is marked as inspection-only and not recomputable.
Causal identification is not claimed; estimates are conditional scenario differences under the stated macroeconomic path, not causal attribution.
Fiscal and agricultural supporting assumptions from historical documents do not transfer to the event pipeline model.
